description: Enforcing civil rights without these reports will be difficult for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, pushing US agency closer to Trump’s agenda, experts warn
Author: Amy Qin
Headline: Enforcing civil rights without these reports will be difficult for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, pushing US agency closer to Trump’s agenda, experts warn
Content: The move represents a fundamental shift for the EEOC.Illustration: Guardian Design/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe move represents a fundamental shift for the EEOC.Illustration: Guardian Design/Getty ImagesDeleted dataTrump administrationThis data has helped fight workplace discrimination for 60 years. The Trump administration plans to delete itEnforcing civil rights without these reports will be difficult for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, pushing US agency closer to Trump’s agenda, experts warnBuilding power is supported byAbout this contentAmy QinWed 2 Sep 2026 11.00 BSTLast modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 18.32 BSTShareThe US civil rights agency mandated to protect equal rights for workers is set to stop collecting data on the demographic makeup of companies – which for the past six decades has been used to enforce anti-discrimination laws.The move marks a fundamental shift for the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC). Without this data, it will be much harder for the agency to identify widespread cases of discrimination in hiring and promotions, experts and former employees of the commission say. And, they warn, it will bring theTrump administrationone step closer toreshapingthe commission from an independent watchdog into an arm of the executive branch narrowly focused on advancing the political grievances ofDonald Trump’s base.Trump 2.0 has deleted or altered nearly 400 US datasets, endangering public health, education and moreRead moreOver the summer, the EEOC proposed terminating its EEO-1 reports, which require companies to submit information on employees, broken down by race, ethnicity, sex and job title. The proposal comes amid the Trump administration’s aggressive attacks on diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) efforts and its consistent work to terminate or alterdecades’ worth of federal datasetsbecause they conflict with its political goals. The majority-Republican commission is expected to approve the measure sometime in the fall.“Getting rid of this data collection is part of a larger effort to weaponize civil rights enforcement and flip the laws that we have on their head,” said Katie Sandson, senior counsel on the education and workplace justice team at the National Women’s Law Center, which is suing the EEOC for refusing to enforce workplace protections for trans employees.The EEO-1 is the only data collection of its kind, providing insights into trends such as the percentage of women in senior level executive positions in US companies and the racial makeup of a company’s lowest-paid staff. With this data, the EEOC, since its creation under the Civil Rights Act of 1964, has investigated thousands of employee complaints every year and helped recover billions of dollars for employees who faced discrimination and harassment.Bar chart showing the gap between employment share of overall workforce versus share of executive roles, by gender and race. White men make up 29% of the workforce but 57% of all executive level positions.But since Trump took office again in January 2025, the EEOC has completely rewritten its strategic goals, and is now prioritizing discrimination claims made bywhitemen,droppingcaseson behalf of transgender workers, investigating workplace diversity practices andrescindinganti-harassment guidance.At a July hearing, Andrea Lucas, the EEOC commissioner who was appointed by Trump, claimed the agency’s demographic data collection was unconstitutional, burdensome on employers, encouraged DEI programs, and incentivized discrimination against white workers.“I believe the Commission’s proposed rescission of the annual reporting requirement will not hinder the Commission’s law enforcement work to investigate specific charges of discrimination,” Lucas said in a statement on the proposed end of the data collection. The EEOC did not respond to the Guardian’s specific questions about how the agency’s priorities have shifted under the secondTrump administration.‘Where there’s smoke, there’s fire’The US agency that fights workplace discrimination just voted to stop measuring it | Jamil SmithRead moreThe EEOC receives nearly 90,000 discrimination complaints every year. EEO-1 data is one of the first tools EEOC investigators use to determine what cases it should put its limited enforcement resources towards, a question that has become especially important at a time when the EEOC’s staffing levels are at their lowest point in 45 years.“If you see a particular employer really stands out because they have fewer women in management or fewer Black people in management compared to their peer employers in the same industry or in the same area, it’s more likely the case that where there’s smoke, there’s fire, and there’s something going on here,” said Karla Gilbride, a former general counsel at the EEOC who is now a deputy director of litigation for the Disability Rights program at the ACLU.The EEO-1 data is also made public in the aggregate (meaning individual employers cannot be identified). For researchers and civil rights advocates, it has been an important source of data to evaluate the impact of diversity and workforce policies.Donald Tomaskovic-Devey, a founding director of the Center for Employment Equity at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, said that he and other researchers have had data-sharing agreements with the EEOC since the late 1990s. Last summer, the EEOC abruptly terminated all data-sharing agreements with social scientists and stopped all communication with them, said Tomaskovic-Devey.Bar chart showing number of cases filed to the EEOC by categoryIn cases when the EEOC can’t settle a complaint with the employer, they can take the employer to court, and EEO-1 data can also be used as supporting evidence in litigation.One such lawsuit started with a complaint filed by Cassandra Coleman. In 2016, she applied for a trucking job at the Phoenix, Arizona, office of Central Transport, a large national trucking company. A male employee tried to discourage her from applying. “It’s not going to do you any good,” he said, according to the complaint. Despite having 21 years of experience and a spotless driving record, Coleman never got a call back from the company. Central Transport hired 10 male truck drivers around the same time.Meet the army of amateur archivists racing to save US history in national parksRead moreThree years later, Coleman applied for another job at Central Transport, this time in Portland, Oregon. She was invited for an interview, but when she arrived at the company offices, she was told the position had been filled.The EEOC found that Coleman wasn’t alone. Female applicants at more than 25 locations across the country alleged their applications to work at Central Transport had been thrown away, lost or passed over for less-qualified male candidates, and together, their cases became part of aclass-action lawsuitfiled by the EEOC.In the lawsuit, the EEOC used the EEO-1 data to show there was a consistent statistical disparity between the number of female truck drivers hired and the number of female applicants, according to the complaint.Combining the data findings with witness testimonies, the agency alleged that Central Transport repeatedly passed over qualified female applicants for more than 10 years and in multiple states. In May 2026, Central Transportagreed to pay$5.5m and enter a consent decree to make changes to its hiring process.A broader attack on diversity, equity and inclusionSince taking office, the Trump administration hasmovedquicklytomaketherollbackof DEI efforts an explicit government objective. Changes at the EEOC have been at the center of this transformation.One of Trump’s first acts during his second term was tofiretwo of the threeDemocratic EEOC commissioners before the end of their five-year terms, an unprecedented move that laid the groundwork for Republicans to gain a 2-1 majority on the commission.In addition to rescinding EEO-1 data collection, the EEOC has sincerolled backguidelines protecting workers from national origin-based discrimination; deleted anti-harassment guidance because itincludedusing the wrong pronouns as harassment,droppedall active cases pertaining to trans or nonbinary people; and announced its intent torevisethe Pregnant Workers Fairness Act to exclude people who need accommodations for abortions and other pregnancy-related medical conditions.Other efforts to root out “DEI-related discrimination” have targeted specific employers. The EEOC openedinvestigationsinto Nike’s corporate diversity practices, sent letters to20 law firmsrequesting information about their DEIpracticesandsuedthe New York Times for allegedly discriminating against a white male employee who did not get promoted.In December, Lucas, the EEOC commissioner, encouraged white men to file discrimination complaints to the EEOC in apost on X. In a video she asks: “Are you a white male who has experienced discrimination at work based on your race or sex? You may have a claim to recover money under federal civil rights laws.”US firms that kept DEI policies despite ‘go woke, go broke’ threats thrivedRead moreFor now, many of the top-down changes appear to have had minimal impact on the types of cases the EEOC is continuing to tackle. “The bulk of EEOC investigator time is still devoted to the ordinary charges they get about ongoing discrimination,” said Chai Feldblum, who was a commissioner from 2010-2019 and is now the president of theEEO Leaders, a watchdog group of former EEOC employees tracking the Trump administration’s actions at the agency.But Feldblum is worried that agency staff are increasingly being pressured to prioritize certain cases based on the agency’s new strategic goals. EEOC stafferstold Mother Joneslast year that they were told to prioritize complaints from workers who allege they were discriminated against for being American-born and stop pursuing gender-identity discrimination cases.In June, the EEOC withdrew its 10-year strategic enforcement plan and instituted a newnational enforcement plan, which explicitly lays out a narrow set of new priorities for the agency: combating “DEI-related discrimination” and “anti-American national origin discrimination”, and protecting “workers’ rights to express the binary nature of sex” and “religious liberty rights”.Getting rid of EEO-1 data is one way to carry out this plan.“The data is not going to show that white people or men are disproportionately not represented in management positions, and so they have no interest in collecting that,” Feldblum said.“It’s not a coincidence that the EEOC is trying to eliminate data collection that documents potential discrimination,” said Maya Raghu, the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law’s director of the Protecting and Advancing Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion initiative.“It’s all part of a bigger pattern of this administration weaponizing our civil rights agencies, both to undermine civil rights protections and enforcement, but also to advance this anti-diversity, equity and inclusion agenda.”The Guardian’s Deleted data series explores how critical US government information is being deleted and what the consequences will be, and will preserve or recreate lost datasets. If you know about any datasets, webpages or government materials that have been deleted or altered in the past year, or are willing to sharehow those changes affect you, we’d love to hear from you. Please reach out atdeleted-data@theguardian.com.

title: My autistic son lives in fear of bailiffs from Ovo breaking into his flat | Money | The Guardian
description: He doesn’t have an account with them but he is being bombarded with demands for money and threats of debt collectors
Author: Anna Tims
Headline: He doesn’t have an account with them but he is being bombarded with demands for money and threats of debt collectors
Content: Ovo Energy sent an agent to the flat to ‘prove’ there was no Ovo meter installed.Photograph: Paul Melling/AlamyView image in fullscreenOvo Energy sent an agent to the flat to ‘prove’ there was no Ovo meter installed.Photograph: Paul Melling/AlamyConsumer championsMoneyMy autistic son lives in fear of bailiffs from Ovo breaking into his flatHe doesn’t have an account with them, but is being bombarded with demands for money and threats of debt collectorsAnna TimsWed 2 Sep 2026 07.00 BSTLast modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 16.18 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMy autistic son has been bombarded for years by letters to his home from OVO Energy addressed to “The Occupier”, with demands for money and threats of debt collectors. He is supplied by Scottish Gas.He was required to let an OVO agent into his flat to “prove” he didn’t have an OVO meter. Neither this, nor countless phone calls, has stopped the demands.Call centre agents confirm that he doesn’t have an account but seem powerless to update the system. He lives in fear that bailiffs will break his door down.LO,EdinburghBritish Gas mixed up our energy meter – but now I’m being penalisedRead moreOVO swiftly decided that the bombardment was triggered by address error on the national database. In short, it says, the gas and electricity meters supplying another property had been registered to your son’s address. It corrected the address for the gas, but tells me another supplier owned the electricity meter and had “rejected multiple requests” by OVO to update the database.In response to my queries, OVO agreed to suspend demands and issued a letter of deadlock to enable your son to complain to the Energy Ombudsman.The letter, which enables access to the database, discovered that the electricity meter was correctly registered to a neighbouring address and supplied by OVO, but OVO had somehow got your son’s address on its billing system. It was ordered to pay £150 compensation and the bills have now ceased.We welcome letters but cannot answer individually. title: Premier League money has lost all meaning amid chaotic spectacle of excess | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: The transfer window has broken all rational rules and limits, leaving us to marvel and, ultimately, pick up the bill
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: The transfer window has broken all rational rules and limits, leaving us to marvel and, ultimately, pick up the bill
Content: Wesley Fofana and Malo Gusto (right) are the only Chelsea players left from the first transfer window of the Clearlake age after exits for Mykhailo Mudryk and Enzo Fernández.Composite: Gaurdian Pictures; Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock; Manchester City FC; Allstar Picture Library/SportsphotoView image in fullscreenWesley Fofana and Malo Gusto (right) are the only Chelsea players left from the first transfer window of the Clearlake age after exits for Mykhailo Mudryk and Enzo Fernández.Composite: Gaurdian Pictures; Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock; Manchester City FC; Allstar Picture Library/SportsphotoTransfer windowPremier League money has lost all meaning amid chaotic spectacle of excessThe transfer window has broken all rational rules and limits, leaving us to marvel and, ultimately, pick up the billBarney RonayWed 2 Sep 2026 20.00 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThere was a research study a few years back into a key period in the life of the TV show Location, Location, Location. You know the one. Half an hour of mid-morning drift. Hosted by two people whose common quality is they both look as if the minced essence of Wellington boots, the Volvo XC40 and the phrase “picky bits” has been reconstituted into human shapes, then sent out to judge people for buying houses.The big reveal was always the bit where they came back a year later and saw how much the value had shifted. Because all conversations about houses are, in the end, an excuse to talk about money. Oh wow, it’s gone up by £20,000. You are good. Oh no, you’re now bankrupt and your flat looks like a hostage cell with fairy lights. Unlucky. You are bad.Premier League transfer talking points: three things we learned from the dataRead moreWhat the study found was that prices basically always increased. Ripping out the stairs, living in a tent in the garden, arguing about what to do with the two-and-a-halfth bedroom – all of this was irrelevant. These were the boom times of the early 2000s, UK housing recast as a global money trap, an endlessly whirling laundromat, a bricks and mortar central bank bond.These people could have bought their run-down three-bed, left it empty and done absolutely nothing for two years. The price would have still gone up. That drama about exactly which shade of Anaconda Breath Morgue And Cakebread Mega-Gloss to use in the underfloor wine cave? Just doesn’t matter. Buy the soil. Shut the door. Let money do its thing.And yes, this is a way of talking aboutthe 2026 summer transfer window, and the way in which everyone has basically now been Chelsea-ed. Think back four years to the start of the age of Clearlake, the first post-Roman spree. At that time it seemed impossible there could be a profitable outcome. Chelsea were out there buying the vintage copper-plate statement bidet. Chelsea were digging out a third sub-basement. Who will redeem this expense? Who will provide a similarly deranged response to such overinvestment?Well, it turns out the market will do this for you. If you’d predicted then that Chelsea would miss out on the Champions League and go through five permanent managers, but still make a profitfrom selling Enzo Fernández, would anyone have believed it?View image in fullscreenTodd Boehly has overseen big changes on and off the pitch during his time at Chelsea.Photograph: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC/Getty ImagesOr that Mykhailo Mudryk could run around briefly like a deranged hamster, get banned for failing a drugs testand still become a potential growth asset? This is pre-subprime crash energy. Yes, you can install a solar-powered mega-wetroom that fires sourdough breadsticks directly into your eyes. Whatever. Ownership is all. Money will take care of you.There are still levels to this. The one Chelsea thing to shift in the window is that the curtain has now been drawn on those initial eight months, the period where Todd Boehly became the world’s worst director of football, a director of football who basically didn’t know what football was.That period has now been safely capped off. Only two players remain. Rough out the numbers and Chelsea spent something like £200m in fees, wages, leaks and cuts, with only Malo Gusto and Wesley Fofana to show for it. No real damage. Money comes, money goes. We roll on.This is the lesson of the latest summer transfer window. Right now it doesn’t really matter what you do in thePremier League. Just being in it is the thing. With one caveat, which is that nobody actually knows what’s happening here. We can marvel at a record window. We can see the biggest spenders are Manchester City on £457.5m, the lowest Crystal Palace on about £50m, the highest net Liverpool on £216.8m. We can pore over Aston Villa buying the bones of a new squad for £56.7m net gain.View image in fullscreenLiverpool’s £123m signing Bradley Barcola checks out Anfield.Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesBut we can’t know what it means, at least not financially. This is part of the design of money on this scale. As the then Federal Reserve chair Alan Greenspan put it in a famous speech on the mysteries of big money: “How do we know when irrational exuberance has unduly escalated asset values, which then become subject to unexpected and prolonged contractions?”Nobody knew what this meant then. Nobody knows what it means now. “Irrational exuberance” is a good phrase, one Greenspan later said came to him in the bath. It was designed to convey the essential point: opacity, vagueness, invisible flows. If not for those actually riding the tide, because someone is always making money. Someone out there actively wants the Premier League’s financial chaos, and is benefiting from it gloriously.Otherwise, reading the runes is just a matter of guesswork. Money moves between networked entities. Everyone inside wins. Everyone outside pays for it. But still, this feels new, if only in its extremity.This was captured by the weirdness of Sky Sports’ transfer deadline programme on Tuesday. At one point a man appeared strumming a guitar, smiling as if he had just filleted a litter of kittens in his basement, and sang a Bradley Barcola Liverpool song to the tune of Don’t Dream It’s Over, like this is all just normal and fine.Later there was a golden period at about 5.30pm where every deal just seemed wrong and impossible, a fever dream after an over-ripe seafood risotto. Aston Villa have paid £47m for an 18-year-old winger. Gabriel Jesus is going to Barcelona. Jack Grealish is having a medical at Everton, an event that seems to prove the non-linear nature of time, a medical that is always happening, never not happening, a constant time-space event.View image in fullscreenGabriel Jesus at his Barcelona unveiling.Photograph: Javier Borrego/AFP7/ShutterstockMeanwhile two private jets are on the tarmac in Lyonas three clubs try to sign Malick Fofana. “We STILL don’t know what Malick Fofana is thinking,” the man with the microphone concluded, mournfully, and this seemed profoundly true and on point. We don’t. Does Malick Fofana even know this? If so, how can he? Nobody else has a clue what’s going on.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIt is worth trying to list the best deals. Harry Wilson on a free can only be good. Djed Spence to Inter is great.Forza, Djed.Barcola to Liverpool for £123mis lots of money, but he’s really young and knows how to score once he’s settled.Newcastle seem to have had a good window, racking up a list of signings that scream inside knowledge and good data, and chime with Matthias Jaissle’s mercurial vibe. Manchester City’s signings have to be good. There’s so many of them, and they’re all excellent players. That midfield is surely just too big to fail.Arsenal will also be fine, despite not signing a 1950s-style hotshot goal ace with dynamite in his boots and the brain of a hungry magpie. Yes, they’ve lost two, maybe three attackers. But these are Jesus and probably Gabriel Martinelli, meat in the room, plus Leandro Trossard, replaced by basically the same guy. Arsenal won the league with Kai Havertz, Martin Ødegaard, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze short of their ceiling. If you can’t score enough to win with that lot then it’s really not the players.Manchester United’s window looks quite good, but also scattergun. Carlos Baleba may be great, or may wander around like a lost child in Lidl before being loaned to Monaco. Tottenham have mined the club’s DNA, gone back to their spiritual roots, and signed players who will be really good for four games, then disappear and get tattoos.Meanwhile Everton have swapped Dwight McNeil for Brennan Johnson. What does it mean? Can you even visualise this as an event? Beto and Iliman Ndiaye have gone, taking away a third of last season’s league goals. Welcome, Everton fans, to the fully immersive Thierno Barry multiverse.Otherwise the main takeaway is the meaninglessness of big football money. Most notably the size of the most basic fees. Little wonder there is a sense of alienation from familiar notions of team building, blocks in place, footballers as recognisable avatars of graft and cultural chemistry. These are stocks, talent units, a flow of resources.View image in fullscreenCaleb Yirenkyi challenges Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly on his Coventry debut, having joined for £23m this summer.Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty ImagesRemember the Peter Odemwingie deadline day fiasco, where Odemwingie sat fuming in his car while the world was sucked into this human drama? That whole thing was about the unbridgeable leap from £2m to £3m. Coventry have just signed Caleb Yirenkyi from Nordsjælland for £23m. Does “Caleb Yirenkyi” really exist? Are you sure?Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club faredRead moreWho pays in the end for this circulation of funds? You, for starters. There is no such thing as football money. It’s all TV rights, state propaganda funds and hard private investment from the kind of people who really don’t give without taking back in the end.On one level books are being balanced, accounting rules satisfied, clubs swapping assets at fees driven in part by regulatory requirements. More obscurely Boehly once talked about a rush of cash being diverted football’s way as a sub-avalanche from quantitative easing in the US, because money just has to go somewhere. No, me neither.All that seems certain is money is being pushed around the board. And that it feels wildly abstract. The window was thrilling, its possibilities endless, a shot of blood for the new season. Beyond this, big football and big finance are playing their own game, in a way that goes beyond the human scale and into a world of pure money. The message below the headlines is clear. This thing belongs to them. Your job, human consumer unit, is simply to look at it and have feelings.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowPremier LeagueFootball politicsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Northampton seek ‘happy medium’ after Hearn claims Pollock worth £1m a year | Northampton | The Guardian
description: Eddie Hearn is pushing for a seven-figure salary for his client, with Phil Dowson, Northampton’s director of rugby, saying ‘the appetite is for him to stay’ but ‘we have to make decisions based on our budget’
Author: Gerard Meagher
Headline: Eddie Hearn is pushing for a seven-figure salary for his client, with Phil Dowson, Northampton’s director of rugby, saying ‘the appetite is for him to stay’ but ‘we have to make decisions based on our budget’
Content: Henry Pollock ‘really wants to stay’ at Northampton according to Saints’ director of rugby, Phil Dowson.Photograph: Dave Winter/INPHO/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenHenry Pollock ‘really wants to stay’ at Northampton according to Saints’ director of rugby, Phil Dowson.Photograph: Dave Winter/INPHO/ShutterstockNorthamptonNorthampton seek ‘happy medium’ after Hearn claims Pollock worth £1m a yearPlayer’s representative pushes for seven-figure salaryPhil Dowson insists ‘the appetite is for him to stay’Gerard MeagherWed 2 Sep 2026 15.44 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheNorthamptondirector of rugby, Phil Dowson, has said the club “have got to find a happy medium” in contract talks with Henry Pollock after the player’s representative, Eddie Hearn, suggested he should be earning £1m a year.Pollock is said to earn around £150,000 a season and his current deal expires at the end of the 2026-27 campaign. Hearn has stated Pollock could earn “10 times” that if he were to move to another club, warning “he can’t stay at the club on the money he’s on”.‘I had no love for myself … now I have peace’: former Ireland rugby player Ryan Caldwell’s journey back from the edgeRead moreThe 21-year-old has 13 England caps but has made only one start. Hearn says his commercial profile warrants a seven-figure salary. Pollock is among the 25 England players to receive an enhanced contract worth £150,000 and Dowson expressed confidencethe Prem championscan keep hold of him.He said: “It is going well. We are still pushing it through. What Eddie Hearn also said, and people have gone straight to the million-pound remark, but the other thing he said is that Henry wants to win stuff, Henry wants to stay at Saints, Henry wants to play with that group of players. He wants to win the World Cup. I embrace that. I am all for that. The appetite is for him to stay. Now we’ve got to find a happy medium. We really want to keep him, he really wants to stay, and that’s a great start.“We still have to make decisions based on our budget and our financial situation. We’ll continue to do that in the best way possible. That is in discussion with agents, discussions with the group and discussions with the decision-makers about what we can afford and how we put a squad together, how that fits within our budget.”Salary cap constraints mean Pollock’s chances of receiving a seven-figure offer are slim, not least because Northampton’s self-imposed budget is significantly less than the cap’s ceiling.Dowson added: “My job is to try and fit 57, 58 players within a squad on a budget. I’ll continue to do that. Eddie Hearn is great for the game, we want to keep Henry Pollock. Fundamentally, nothing has changed. What he says is based on his job.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“Eddie Hearn has a job to do, and that is to promote his client and ask for more money for his client. He’s doing both of those very effectively. We’ve said we want to publicise and grow the game and he has the ability to do that.”Explore more on these topicsNorthamptonRugby unionnewsShareReuse this content

title: Championship roundup: Wrexham rout Millwall to seal first league victory | Championship | The Guardian
description: Kieffer Moore and Jacques Ekomié were on target in Wrexham’s 3-0 win at Millwall, while QPR beat Cardiff and Middlesbrough drew at Burnley
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kieffer Moore and Jacques Ekomié were on target in Wrexham’s 3-0 win at Millwall, while QPR beat Cardiff and Middlesbrough drew at Burnley
Content: Jacques Ekomié wheels away in delight after scoring Wrexham’s third goal at Millwall.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenJacques Ekomié wheels away in delight after scoring Wrexham’s third goal at Millwall.Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty ImagesChampionshipChampionship roundup: Wrexham rout Millwall to seal first league victoryKieffer Moore and Jacques Ekomié score in 3-0 winQPR beat Cardiff; Middlesbrough draw at BurnleyAgence France-PresseWed 2 Sep 2026 23.10 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 00.19 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWrexhampowered to their firstChampionshipwin this season with a ruthless 3-0 rout of injury-plaguedMillwallon Wednesday.The Welsh side had drawn with Cardiff and Watford before losing at home to Birmingham prior to this match. But they bounced back in emphatic fashion in south London to kickstart their bid for promotion to the Premier League after narrowly missing out on the playoffs last term.West Ham fight off Wolves as Divine Mukasa double eases pressure on NunoRead moreTheMillwalldefender Zak Sturge deflected Issa Kaboré’s cross into his own net for a first-half own goal. Wrexham’s striker Kieffer Moore lashed in the second from 20 yards soon after half-time and Jacques Ekomié wrapped up the victory with a close-range finish.After starting with two clean sheets in victories over Bristol City and Norwich, it is now eight goals conceded in two games for Millwall, who were thrashed 5-1 by Southampton on Saturday. Millwall lost their striker Josh Coburn and midfielder Casper De Norre to injuries during the game as their fitness woes mounted 24 hours after Nigeria winger Femi Azeez joined Brighton for £15m.Rumarn Burrell scored both goals asQPRbeatCardiff2-1 at Loftus Road to extend their impressive start to the season.Perry Ng pulled a goal back for Cardiff but it was not enough to stop Julien Stéphan’s second-placed side from moving to 10 points from their opening four matches.Ugo Raghouber’s first goal forBurnleyearned them only their second point from four matches as they came from behind to draw 1-1 withMiddlesbroughat Turf Moor.The French midfielder, signed from Lille in July, steered in a 54th-minute equaliser from Zeki Amdouni’s pass. Aidan Morris had swept Middlesbrough into a 23rd-minute lead, scoring his first goal after more than two years at the club, with a stylish finish from 20 yards.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRelegated from the Premier League last season,Burnleyare in a testing period that included a 4-1 loss at Norwich last Saturday and the sale of the Dutch forward Zian Flemming to Ipswich on transfer deadline day.Charltonlost their 100% record but remain unbeaten after Tyreece Campbell’s second-half strike secured a 1-1 draw atWest Brom. Nathan Jones’s side trailed to a thunderous Callum Styles strike just before the hour mark, before Campbell fired home from close-range on 69 minutes.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipWrexhamMillwallQPRCardiff CityBurnleyMiddlesbroughnewsShareReuse this content

title: England omit Brydon Carse again for third Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston | England cricket team | The Guardian
description: The Durham seamer was also dropped from the squad for the second Test after a late-night incident in a Derby bar last month
Author: Simon Burnton
Headline: The Durham seamer was also dropped from the squad for the second Test after a late-night incident in a Derby bar last month
Content: The Durham bowler Brydon Carse has been left out of England’s latest Test squad.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAView image in fullscreenThe Durham bowler Brydon Carse has been left out of England’s latest Test squad.Photograph: Mike Egerton/PAEngland cricket teamEngland omit Brydon Carse again for third Test against Pakistan at EdgbastonCarse also missed second Test after incident in Derby barMatthew Fisher absence is only change from Lord’s squadSimon BurntonWed 2 Sep 2026 18.56 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBrydon Carse has been left out of England’s squad for the final Test of the summer, against Pakistan at Edgbaston next week, with police still investigating allegations of an assault connected with thelate-night incident at a Derby bar last monththat led to the Durham seamer being briefly arrested and placed in handcuffs. The Cricket Regulator is also investigating the incident.As a result of the allegations, and with investigations ongoing, Carse was dropped from the squad for last week’s second Test. The 31-year-old had been in the squad for the first game, but not named in the XI. Sonny Baker, who replaced him for the second Test but also did not play, remains in a squad that has changed only by the absence of Matthew Fisher. Alongside Baker, the other squad members who were not in the team at Lord’s are Shoaib Bashir, Sam Cook and Ollie Pope.Joe Root urges England to celebrate Pakistan series win in ‘sensible, grown-up way’Read moreAfter England sealed the series win withvictory at Lord’sMarcus Trescothick, the interim coach, promised that “we’re not going to ease off the gas” and spoke of the benefit the side’s current first-choice seamers – Jofra Archer, Ollie Robinson, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson – would get from regularly playing together. “The more experience everyone gets together, then it sort of fits into place how you want it to be.”But if England are likely to be unchanged the same is not true of their opponents, who announced on Monday that they hadsacked Sarfaraz Ahmed, their head coach, and were immediately dropping seven players, of whom five had played in at least one of the first two Tests. Given they had 18 players in their original squad it is theoretically possible for them to not pick any of their seven replacements, of whom five are currently uncapped, though the outgoing players include two of their four bowlers and both recognised all-rounders.Quick GuideEngland squad for third TestShowJoe Root(Yorkshire, captain),Jofra Archer(Sussex),Gus Atkinson(Surrey),Sonny Baker(Hampshire),Shoaib Bashir(Derbyshire),Harry Brook(Yorkshire),Sam Cook(Essex),Jordan Cox(Essex),Ben Duckett(Nottinghamshire),Emilio Gay(Durham),Dan Lawrence(Surrey),Ollie Pope(Surrey),Ollie Robinson(Sussex),Jamie Smith(Surrey),Josh Tongue(Nottinghamshire)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Should the final Test go to five days England will then have less than 48 hours to prepare for a white-ball series against Sri Lanka starting on 15 September in Southampton. Sri Lanka announced their squad for both T20 and ODI series on Wednesday, with Charith Asalanka – who replaced Kusal Mendis as captain in 2024 but was himself replaced when Mendis returned to the role earlier this year, as well as being dropped from the T20 squad – back as vice-captain in both formats.Asalanka’s return is reward for his form in this year’s Lanka Premier League, the country’s domestic T20 competition, in which he scored 385 runs in the tournament and was named player of the match in last month’s final. Lahiru Udara, the top-scorer in the LPL with 434 runs, is recalled three years after his one previous appearance. England are expected to announce their squad for the series later this week.Explore more on these topicsEngland cricket teamCricketEngland v Pakistan 2026Pakistan cricket teamnewsShareReuse this content

title: Vuelta a España: Britain’s Brennan seals hat-trick of stage wins as Mas retains lead | Vuelta a España | The Guardian
description: Matthew Brennan triumphed on stage 11 of the Vuelta a España, becoming the first cyclist to win three stages in his first Grand Tour since Tadej Pogacar
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Matthew Brennan triumphed on stage 11 of the Vuelta a España, becoming the first cyclist to win three stages in his first Grand Tour since Tadej Pogacar
Content: Matthew Brennan of Team Visma-Lease a Bike reacts after winning his third stage on this year’s Vuelta a España.Photograph: Javier Lizón/EPAView image in fullscreenMatthew Brennan of Team Visma-Lease a Bike reacts after winning his third stage on this year’s Vuelta a España.Photograph: Javier Lizón/EPAVuelta a EspañaVuelta a España: Britain’s Brennan seals hat-trick of stage wins as Mas retains leadStage 11 won by 21-year-old as dazzling debut continuesLewis Askey claims opening stage in Tour of BritainAgenciesWed 2 Sep 2026 18.34 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMatthew Brennan triumphed again in theVuelta a Españaon Wednesday, becoming the first cyclist to win three stages in his first Grand Tour since Tadej Pogacar seven years ago. The British rider secured his third victory on the 11th stage, a mostly flat route of 153.8km from Cartagena to Lorca.“We took the initiative today again,” Brennan said. “The boys pulled as hard as they could even after a tough day in the legs yesterday. We still went full gas. Coming into the final, we really held our own place and knew that we were all strong enough to kind of get to where we want to be.”US cyclist Ezra Caudell hospitalized with ‘multi-system trauma’ after Philadelphia crashRead moreThe 21-year-old of team Visma-Lease a Bike also won the second and fifth stages to become the youngest cyclist with multiple stage wins in the Vuelta since Pogacar’s three victories in 2019.“It’s massive [to have won three stages],” Brennan said. “I’m with a team full of massive champions. We’ve got guys who have podiumed in Grand Tours and won them as well, and guys who’ve won classics and huge races. And the fact they go for me is an amazing opportunity. I’m really thankful that they go full gas for me.”A sprinter had not claimed at least three victories in his maiden Grand Tour since Fernando Gaviria in the Giro d’Italia in 2017. Pogacar also had already won three stages in this year’s Vuelta beforea crash forced him to withdrawon Saturday while holding a big overall lead. He fractured his left collarbone and could not continue on his quest for a career sweep of the three Grand Tours.Enric Mas, from Movistar Team, took the overall lead from Pogacar and has kept it since. He is 1min 18sec ahead of Primoz Roglic, from team Red Bull-Bora Hansgrohe. Roglic is chasing a record fifth Vuelta title.On Thursday, riders will face a 12th stage featuring a tough mountain route in southern Spain. It includes a traditional double climb at Velefique and Calar Alto, marking an important day for the riders fighting for the general classification.The three-week Vuelta finishes in Granada on 13 September.Britain’s Lewis Askey, meanwhile, won the opening stage of theTour of Britain, the NSN rider attacking on the cobbles of the Michaelgate climb in Lincoln and riding clear to victory. The Italian Filippo Ganna of Netcompany Ineos came home second, two seconds down, while the Belgian Tim Wellens of UAE Team Emirates-XRG was third.View image in fullscreenLewis Askey leads the way on the cobbles in Lincoln.Photograph: Zac Williams/SWpix.com/Shutterstock“It feels amazing, especially to have my grandparents there at the finish line. It was super special,” said Askey. “I ride my bike to win races. It’s great when you come second, come third and do good performances, but nothing matches managing to put your hands up in the air.”Explore more on these topicsVuelta a EspañaCyclingTour of BritainnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tiger Woods handed five-year driving ban after no-contest plea over crash | Tiger Woods | The Guardian
description: Golf star avoids jail after DUI charge is reduced and receives five-year driving ban following March rollover crash
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Golf star avoids jail after DUI charge is reduced and receives five-year driving ban following March rollover crash
Content: In this image from police body camera video, Tiger Woods performs a field sobriety test following a car crash on Jupiter Island, Florida, on 27 March 2026.Photograph: Martin County Sheriff's Office/APView image in fullscreenIn this image from police body camera video, Tiger Woods performs a field sobriety test following a car crash on Jupiter Island, Florida, on 27 March 2026.Photograph: Martin County Sheriff's Office/APTiger WoodsTiger Woods handed five-year driving ban after no-contest plea over crashWoods pleads no contest to reduced chargeCharges stemmed from March rollover crashGuardian sportand agenciesWed 2 Sep 2026 14.25 BSTFirst published on Wed 2 Sep 2026 05.35 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTiger Woods pleaded no contest to reckless driving on Wednesday morning as part of an agreement with Florida prosecutors that reduced a DUI charge stemmingfrom his rollover crash in March.The 50-year-old was adjudicated guilty of willful and wanton reckless driving, a second offense, during a hearing in Martin County court. Under the agreement, Woods was fined $1,000 and had his driver’s license suspended for five years. Prosecutors had originally charged him with driving under the influence with property damage.Woods also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to a lawful test and was fined $500 on that count. He received a concurrent five-year license suspension on a careless-driving citation and agreed not to seek a hardship exemption during the suspension. Court records show he paid $2,131.44 in fines and costs following Wednesday’s hearing.The plea agreement brings an end to the criminal case arising from the golfer’s crash near hisFloridahome on Jupiter Island. He had previously pleaded not guilty to both charges.Tiger Woods’ latest brush with the law leaves questions why golf remains so beholden to him | Ewan MurrayRead moreWoods, dressed in ⁠a dark suit and tie, arrived at the Martin County Courthouse seated in the front passenger seat of ​a black SUV. He did not answer questions ‌from the gathered reporters as ‌he and his girlfriend, Vanessa Trump, walked in and out of the building for the change of plea hearing.The charges stemmed from a 27 March crash in Hobe Sound. Martin County sheriff John Budensiek said Woods was driving a Land Rover that overturned after he attempted to overtake a truck on a narrow two-lane road shortly before 2pm.The truck had been slowing to turn into a driveway when Woods approached at what Budensiek described as a “high rate of speed” on a road with a 30mph limit. Woods’s vehicle clipped a trailer, veered off and came to rest on its driver’s side after sliding along the roadway.Woods, who was alone in the vehicle, was able to exit through the passenger side and was not injured. Investigators said he showed signs of impairment and subjected him to roadside tests before taking him into custody.A breath test showed no alcohol in his system, but Woods refused to provide a urine sample for drug testing. He told investigators he had taken several medications earlier that day, including drugs for high blood pressure and cholesterol as well as ibuprofen and the prescription painkiller Vicodin, according to court filings released by prosecutors.The filings alsodetailed a series of unusual remarksWoods made to officers at the scene. About an hour after the crash, he spoke of “10 to 15 drones” equipped with GoPro cameras flying over his home and car. At another point, after stepping away while on the phone, Woods told an officer he had “just [been] talking to the president” before trailing off. The documents did not identify which president he meant, although Donald Trump said later that day that he had spoken with Woods following the crash.Woods also told officers he had been looking down at his phone to change the radio station when the collision occurred.3:01Bodycam footage shows moment Tiger Woods is arrested for DUI – videoProsecutors later sought access to Woods’s prescription records from the months leading up to the crash. His attorneys objected, arguing that the records were private, and asked a judge to determine whether they were relevant to the case and to restrict their disclosure.Days after his arrest, Woods announcedthat he would step away from golf“to seek treatment and focus on my health”. A judge subsequently granted him permission to travel abroad to enter an inpatient treatment facility, which his attorney said was necessary for an intensive, individualized program.The crash marked another high-profile traffic incident for Woods. In February 2021,he was seriously injuredwhen his SUV veered off a road in Los Angeles at high speed, leaving him with leg and ankle injuries so severe that doctors considered amputation.He was alsoarrested on a DUI chargein south Florida in 2017 after police found him asleep behind the wheel of a damaged vehicle. Woods later said he had taken a problematic combination of prescription medications and pleaded guilty to reckless driving.Another incident took place in 2009, when Woods crashed his SUV into a fire hydrant and a tree outside his home in Windermere, Florida.Woods has played a limited schedule in recent years amid chronic pain, injuries and multiple surgeries, including a seventh back procedure and a ruptured achilles tendon. He has not competed in an official PGA Tour event since July 2024.An 82-time winner on the PGA Tour, Woods is tied with Sam Snead for the most victories in tour history. The 15-time major champion last won one at the 2019 Masters, his fifth title at Augusta National.Explore more on these topicsTiger WoodsGolfFloridaUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Lando Norris launches LN4 Fusion team to develop young drivers in F1 and motorsport | Lando Norris | The Guardian
description: The F1 champion became the first to back a team in the junior single-seater era and also created a legacy programme to support talent
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: The F1 champion became the first to back a team in the junior single-seater era and also created a legacy programme to support talent
Content: Lando Norris has co-founded a new junior, single-seater racing team.Photograph: LN4 FusionView image in fullscreenLando Norris has co-founded a new junior, single-seater racing team.Photograph: LN4 FusionLando NorrisLando Norris launches LN4 Fusion team to develop young drivers in F1 and motorsportF1 champion first to back junior team in single-seater eraNorris also creates legacy programme to support talentGiles RichardsWed 2 Sep 2026 19.06 BSTLast modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 19.08 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLando Norris has co-founded a new junior, single-seater racing team. Named LN4 Fusion it will compete in multiple championships including the feeder series for Formula One, F3 and F2, asthe current F1 world championcommits to helping young drivers make it to the top level in motorsport.Norris’s involvement, including a personal financial undertaking alongside an investment group, represents the first time an F1 world champion has directly backed a team in the modern junior single-seater era. As part of the project he has also established the LN4 Legacy programme, a driver development initiative designed to identify and support talent coming through the ranks from karting upwards and then provide assistance financially as well as in coaching, performance and career support.Lando Norris agrees new deal until at least 2030 with ‘second family’ McLarenRead moreThe McLaren driverlaunched the project at an event in Monza, which will host the Italian Grand Prix this weekend. It constitutes a serious and comprehensive effort to address some of the difficulties facing junior drivers coming through the ranks, which Norris has previously identified as a fundamental problem for the sport.“I know that getting toFormula Onetakes so much more than just talent. You need the right people around you, the right support and the right opportunities at the right time,” he said.“That’s what these two projects are all about. LN4 Fusion is about building a race team that can compete with the best in junior motorsport, with great people and a great environment for drivers to develop. The LN4 Legacy programme is about helping talented young drivers get opportunities they might not otherwise have.“They naturally fit together. I want to help create opportunities for the next generation both on and off the track and hopefully make a real difference to young drivers coming through the sport.”View image in fullscreenLando Norris became the world champion with McLaren in 2025.Photograph: Clive Mason/Getty ImagesThe intent for the LN4 Fusion team will be to compete across a range of championships as of next year with already confirmed programmes in F3 for 2027, as well as the Italian F4 Championship and the FIA Formula Regional European Championship. As part of the process the team has acquired key assets from the German team AIX Racing, which has an F3 entry until the end of the 2027 season and has applied for participation in the F2 Championship.Norris will play an active role in the organisation and his role was welcomed by the F1 chief executive, Stefano Domenicali. “SeeingLando Norrisinvolved in this new project is an incredible statement on how much the pyramid of Formula 3 and Formula 2 is crucial to the future of Formula One,” he said. “Through Lando’s investment and experience we can build a future, with new drivers, engineers, mechanics, and a tradition that will be followed by motorsport lovers.”The seriousness of Norris’s ambition was emphasised with the appointment of René Rosin as team principal. Rosin was formerly the principal and managing director of the Prema team, which has enjoyed more than 40 years of competition in the junior series. They have won multiple titles and are one of the go-to teams for developing young talent. Prema brought on many drivers who went on to F1 including, among others on the current grid, the championship leader, Kimi Antonelli, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc as well as Norris’sMcLarenteammate Oscar Piastri. The team also nurtured Jacques Villeneuve who went on to take the F1 title.Part of the LN4 Fusion team will be formed from the experience and personnel at the Fusion Motorsport team, which has enjoyed huge success for 25 years in UK karting, with multiple national and more recently international titles. The head of Fusion Motorsport karting, Dan Hazlewood, will be team principal of the LN4 Fusion UK operation, including overseeing the planned entry into the British F4 championship and in bringing talent through from karting.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenLando Norris’s LN4 Fusion F3 car.Photograph: LN4 FusionWith 2027 set for the opening of racing for the team, the organisation is developing a European headquarters in Veneto, northern Italy with a British base in Cambridgeshire already developing the F4 programme.Rosin emphasised the importance of having Norris as a key part of the new venture and its expectations of success.“Having Lando on board adds a further dimension to this project,” he said. “He has come through the junior single-seater ranks and understands its demands. His involvement will make a real difference to the team. We want to develop a pathway through junior single-seaters and create an environment in which drivers, engineers and sporting personnel can perform at the highest level.”The chief executive, Dan Richards, echoed the optimism, believing they had all the requisite elements for success in place. “What we have created is far more than simply the acquisition of a racing team,” he said.“We have assembled a rare combination and secured the right sporting leadership in the industry: an established operation, a Formula One world champion, the most successful team principal in junior single-seater racing over the past two decades, world-class motorsport expertise, significant investment and a shared ambition to build a team capable of competing at the highest levels of the sport.”Explore more on these topicsLando NorrisMcLarenFormula OneFormula One 2026Motor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Walsh caps Champions League progress for Chelsea despite Real Sociedad grind | Women's Champions League | The Guardian
description: Keira Walsh scored at a corner to earn Chelsea a 1-0 win against Real Sociedad in San Sebastián and settle a hard-fought tie
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Keira Walsh scored at a corner to earn Chelsea a 1-0 win against Real Sociedad in San Sebastián and settle a hard-fought tie
Content: Chelsea celebrate after Keira Walsh scores the only goal of the game.Photograph: Gari Garaialde/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenChelsea celebrate after Keira Walsh scores the only goal of the game.Photograph: Gari Garaialde/Getty ImagesWomen's Champions LeagueWalsh caps Champions League progress for Chelsea despite Real Sociedad grindReal Sociedad 0-1 Chelsea (agg 2-6)Keira Walsh scores at corner to settle tieSuzanne WrackWed 2 Sep 2026 20.54 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleChelsea ensured there will be three Women’s Super League teams in the league phase of the Champions League as Keira Walsh’s second-half strike against Real Sociedad extended their three-goal margin from the first leg of the third-round qualifier.The5-2 winagainst the Spanish side in Chelsea’s first game at Wimbledon’s Cherry Red Records stadium gave Sonia Bompastor’s side a commanding lead in the tie, after a rusty start had forced them to come from a goal down. It wasn’t a particularly pretty performance, though, and that continued into the second leg againstLa Real, who will now drop into the Europa League.Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 6: ChelseaRead moreBompastor, who returned to the dugout after serving a one-match ban in the reverse game, made four changes for the trip to San Sebastián, probably with one eye on the WSL opener on Saturday against Aston Villa. The scorer of Chelsea’s second last week, Veerle Buurman, was named on the bench, alongside Katie McCabe, Sjoeke Nüsken and Alyssa Thompson. Among those to come in was the 20-year-old midfielder Lexi Potter, who scored in her first league start for Chelsea, a 2-1 win against Brighton, in March.There were only two changes for the home team. The change that mattered most, though, was the one that had taken place in the ­dugout. In between these two critical ­Champions League qualifying games, Arturo Ruiz, the Real Sociedad ­manager, exited andwas unveiled as the new Brighton managerfollowing the shock departure of Dario Vidosic. If Vidosic’s exit had been a surprise, Brighton poaching Ruiz was a bigger one. Gorka Álvarez, who left Real Sociedad in 2025 following three seasons managing the reserves and a year as an assistant to SD Eibar’s women’s team, was hurriedly brought in to lead them in their Liga F opener against Logroño on Saturday, a 2-0 loss, and the second leg against Chelsea.It was a mountain of a task ­facing the 40-year-old and, in many respects, a bit of a free hit, with few expecting Real Sociedad to come close to overturning a three-goal ­deficit against European heavyweights.However, setting the tone for his tenure and building confidence was important.La Realdid well against the visitors, holding Bompastor’s side at bay until Walsh swept in from a corner in the 54th minute to kill any outlandish hopes there may have been of a comeback.Until then, the London side ­struggled to create clear chances withLa Realmirroring their well-organised display in the first half of the first leg.Ellie Carpenter, playing further forward, ahead of Lucy Bronze on the right, was Chelsea’s best outlet but they couldn’t capitalise on her balls into the middle. Walsh’s side-footed effort in the first half was weak and easy for the goalkeeper Julia Arrula. Aggie Beever-Jones had a good chance to break the deadlock moments before Walsh’s goal but the forward’s strike was too central and Arrula made an easy save.The perfectionist that Bompastor is, she will be unhappy with the nature of the two games, but the reality is that reaching the league phase, for a team desperately wanting European glory, was what mattered most. In the end the result was comfortable, even if the performance wasn’t, and Chelsea had the chance to give debuts off the bench to their new signings Nelly Las and Giulia Dragoni, and minutes to the talented 17-year-old Chloe Sarwie.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThey will have also benefited from valuable competitive minutes before they kickstart their WSL campaign by hosting Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge on Saturday.Bompastor said: “Today we gave some really good opportunities to the young players to come and experience a Champions League game, so when you have the opportunity to do that, I think it’s always something really positive. I’m happy and really excited now to be in the Champions League this season. The goal was for us to qualify, which is what we have done.”On Friday 4 September at 1pm Suzanne Wrack will be answering readers’ questions about the new WSL season for GuardianConversationsExplore more on these topicsWomen's Champions LeagueChelsea WomenWomen's footballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Maro Itoje ready to ‘come back better’ for England after taking mini sabbatical | Rugby union | The Guardian
description: Maro Itoje, who sat out England’s Nations Championship games in July, is healthy and mentally rested after a rare full pre-season with Saracens
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: Maro Itoje, who sat out England’s Nations Championship games in July, is healthy and mentally rested after a rare full pre-season with Saracens
Content: Maro Itoje is now feeling the benefits of ‘taking a breath’ after an intense year on and off the field.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenMaro Itoje is now feeling the benefits of ‘taking a breath’ after an intense year on and off the field.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianRugby unionMaro Itoje ready to ‘come back better’ for England after taking mini sabbaticalItoje rested for Nations Championship games in JulyCaptain has had a rare full pre-season with SaracensRobert KitsonWed 2 Sep 2026 17.00 BSTLast modified on Thu 3 Sep 2026 02.30 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMaro Itoje says it felt “very weird” watching England play from afar this summer but he believes more top players should consider taking a break to prolong their careers. The British & Irish Lions captain was rested for his country’s three Nations Championship games in July and is now feeling the benefits of “taking a breath” after an intense year on and off the field.In addition to the burden of leadership for club and country, Itoje also lost his mother last year and, with the 2027 World Cup looming, the national coach, Steve Borthwick, offered his captain the chance of a mini-sabbatical. He has emerged fit, healthy and mentally rested for the season ahead having enjoyed his first full club pre-season atSaracenssince 2014.Lawrence and Daly lose England central contracts as Borthwick looks to World CupRead more“I don’t regret it at all,” Itoje said at the Prem media launch at Twickenham. “In some respects it was a little bit weird being away from the team, especially whilst games were going on. But at the same time I felt like it was the right thing to do. Mentally it was a busy year, both personally and professionally, so it was nice to have a bit of time to take a breath.”Coincidentally, Itoje bumped into the England squad at Heathrow airport on the day they were returning from theSouth African leg of their tourbut otherwise he did his best to keep his distance, even choosing not to watch the games live to avoid getting too emotionally involved. “When you watch a game live, you’re in every nook and cranny, every tackle. But that also probably has a hidden emotional kind of weight. I felt it would have defeated the purpose of what I was trying to achieve.”Itoje, who turns 32 next month, would certainly recommend a break to other leading players as and when the chance arises, with South Africa and New Zealand having long since pursued a policy of allowing their top stars to sign contracts in Japan. “It is very much case by case but I think that, for players who have the blessing to be at the top of the game for a period of time, a proactive approach like this one works.“I was taken aback initially because it just never entered my mind. It was never something that I thought was an option … I kind of had it in my mind that ‘this is the way the cookie crumbles’ and you just have to power through. [But] the more I thought about it, the more I kind of agreed with it. If I was not going to do it then I’m not sure when the next window would have been.”View image in fullscreenMaro Itoje kept his distance during his break, even choosing not to watch England games live to avoid getting too emotionally involved.Photograph: Dan Mullan/The RFU Collection/Getty ImagesThe next challenge is to hit the ground running when the Prem season kicks off this month before a busy November. England are scheduled to play four Tests on successive weekends, starting with a game against Australia on 8 November, and a refreshed Itoje will be keen to make an immediate impact.“I hope the break is giving me what’s necessary for me to come back better. Since I’ve been involved with England, I’ve pretty much been involved in every campaign. Saracens for a large period of that time were the top team in Europe, so we’re going deep into Europe and deep in the Premiership. And that has also helped with Lions tours and selections.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I’ve been very fortunate to have had what I’ve had but the cost of that, I guess, is that you don’t tend to have a break. Apart from missing training today, I’ve had a full pre-season [with Saracens] to work on myself and my body and be around the team, and I think that’s been a good thing.”Itoje will soon have added responsibilities on his plate with his wife, Mimi, who is pregnant with the couple’s first child – but on the England front he says he was encouraged by what he saw towards the end of England’s summer Tests under the leadership of his Saracens teammate Jamie George. “I was delighted with the last two results,” he said.“Obviously theFiji game was a big winand in the Argentina game they showed a lot of character away from home. The challenge and opportunity for us now is to build on that to go forward.”Explore more on these topicsRugby unionMaro ItojeEngland rugby union teamPrem RugbySaracensnewsShareReuse this content

title: Old master Gooch offers hope for modern great Root in battle against lbws | Cricket | The Guardian
description: Batting is all about solving problems, and the grand old man of Essex backs the England captain to find a way past this one – just like he did
Author: James Wallace
Headline: Batting is all about solving problems, and the grand old man of Essex backs the England captain to find a way past this one – just like he did
Content: Joe Root has become more used than he would like to the ball thudding into his front pad this summer.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAView image in fullscreenJoe Root has become more used than he would like to the ball thudding into his front pad this summer.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAThe Spin newsletterCricketOld master Gooch offers hope for modern great Root in battle against lbwsBatting is all about solving problems, and the grand old man of Essex backs the England captain to find a way past this one – just like he didJames WallaceWed 2 Sep 2026 10.26 BSTLast modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 22.40 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJoe Root lets out a “Woaaa-ho!” as a ball from Pakistan’s Mohammad Ali angles in and then jags away late at Lord’s on the evening of day two. The ball flies past Root’s batting gloves and thuds into Mohammed Rizwan’s keeping ones at head height behind the stumps. Rizwan is stood back too, not up to the stumps and breathing down Root’s neckin the summer 2026 way of things.Root offers that impish smile and shakes his head at the deviousness of the delivery. He isn’t smiling after the next ball. Ali pushes his follow-up fuller, it doesn’t zip and lift away but darts back and scuds low, pinning Root on the pad. He reviews with a weary shrug but he knows his fate – it’s his second lbw dismissal in the Test, his seventh of the summer and ninth in his past 12 innings.After 15 years and more than 14,000 runs, does Joe Root have an lbw problem? Is this the ghost ofDavey Warner’s surfboard? Will the wobble seam and keeper-up combo change the face of the Test game irrevocably? Is the sky falling in?Root’s post-match comments when asked the inevitable tell us plenty. With a glint in his eye he gave an insight into why he is one of the all-time greats: “I’ve played this game a long time, I’ve always found ways of solving those problems and working it through and I don’t see this as being any different.”View image in fullscreenJoe Root has not scored a Test hundred for 10 innings, going back to his 160 in the final Test of the Ashes in Sydney.Photograph: Jono Searle/AAPThere was more than a whiff of “events, dear boy, events” about his answers.Root has been here before, from the teenage growth spurt that destroyed his technique to the only recently answered questions about hislack of a Test ton in Australia. Batting with the captaincy. Batting without the captaincy.Batting with the captaincy, again. Root finds a way.Elite batting is an endless series of riddles to be solved, Escher staircases to be climbed, heavy-duty safes to be cracked. The job is never done, there’s never a sense of completion. Root isn’t quite Sisyphus with a New Balance blade because he actually relishes the work – the boulder feels good, the leg-befores make you think. Fixing one technical thing in a batting technique often reveals or directly results in a flaw in another, which is what makes it perpetually compelling and maddening.Root did admit that he was “frustrated” with the lbw trend and knows full well that a couple more similar dismissals at Edgbaston will only lead to more loose-lipped lbw chat. He knows the caveats are there, that the balls are zipping,the pitches are seamingand the keepers are lurking. The number of lbw dismissals in Tests this summer is at 23% compared to the constant 13 % from 2021-2025.As Root said himself, a handful of his seven this summer so far could have gone either way on DRS. Not that the bowlers or the scorebook care.One thing for which Root could be thankful is that his lbw dismissals have not all been at the hands of one man. “I went through three pairs of pads because of him,” Graham Gooch says with a laugh as he recalls hispaddus horribilisagainst Australia’s Terry Alderman in the English summer of 1989.For a few months the ursine run machine found himself cast as a doomed sentinel in white helmet caught in an endless cycle of ball-pad-finger-trudge. An apocryphal piece of graffiti at the time apparently read “Thatcher Out!” with “lbw bowled Alderman” added below.Cricketcould only hope for that sort of cut-through these days.When the Spin calls Gooch to ask him about that Ashes series his phone at first goes to voicemail. That unmistakable Essex falsetto clicks in: “I’m afraid our team’s all out, please leave a message …”View image in fullscreenGraham Gooch (left) spoke to the England team before the second Test against Pakistan – it is unknown whether the lbw travails of Joe Root (right) were part of the speech.Photograph: Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesWhich raises the question of whether another bit of cricketing lore is actually true, that he changed his answerphone message that summer to “I’m out, probably to Terry bloody Alderman …”Sadly, Gooch confirms that one is untrue, recalling that at the time he wasn’t in the mood to joke: “My technique wasn’t where I wanted it to be and I needed to straighten it out.” Gooch is adamant his situation is different from Root’s: “He’ll find a way, that’s why he’s world class. Top players generally get out lbw or nick off. They don’t get bowled or caught in the ring and that sort of stuff. Joe falls into that category. So, you know, it’s causing him a little bit of an irritation, but that’s the life of a batter.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe SpinSubscribe to our cricket newsletter for our writers' thoughts on the biggest stories and a review of the week’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGooch went to see his old opening partner Geoffrey Boycott to help iron out his technical batting difficulties. “I was playing across the line a little bit too much and I made the mistake of moving more to the leg side,” he recalls. “All I was doing then was moving further across the crease laterally from leg to off, which made it worse.“I straightened up; instead of taking a leg stump guard I went across to middle, middle and leg, and I just moved my back foot backwards. It was instantly a lot better. It was less movement; the less movement the better and you don’t want to be moving laterally.”He lets out a high-pitched chuckle before adding: “It’s like Ted Dexter said, and it’s still spot on – ‘bat like you are stood in a bath (forward and back, not sideways), not a pisspot (no feet movement at all).”Gooch doesn’t see any such flaws in Root’s technique and stresses again not to conflate the two. The man who has scoredmore professional runs than anyone elsein the history of the game then sums up the batter’s relentless paradigm: “You encounter endless problems, it’s all about how you are equal to them and how you come through them. If you work one thing out and think it’s all going to be rosy, well no, it doesn’t work like that. You’re always going to have things that are going to challenge you.”You can imagine the glint in his eye as he says it.This is an extract from the Guardian’s weekly cricket email, The Spin.To subscribe, just visit this page and follow the instructions.Explore more on these topicsCricketThe Spin newsletternewslettersShareReuse this content

title: Clippers docked five first-round draft picks and fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandal | Los Angeles Clippers | The Guardian
description: The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Clippers after finding the franchise circumvented salary cap rules
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Clippers after finding the franchise circumvented salary cap rules
Content: Kawhi Leonard signed for the Clippers in 2019.Photograph: Matt Slocum/APView image in fullscreenKawhi Leonard signed for the Clippers in 2019.Photograph: Matt Slocum/APLos Angeles ClippersClippers docked five first-round draft picks and fined $30m over Kawhi Leonard scandalTeam circumvented salary cap rules to sign starOwner Steve Ballmer lands one-year banGuardian sportWed 2 Sep 2026 21.52 BSTLast modified on Wed 2 Sep 2026 22.36 BSTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe NBA has handed down one of the biggest punishments in the history of the league to the Los Angeles Clippers after finding that the franchisecircumvented salary cap ruleswhen it courted Kawhi Leonard as a free agent.The league has stripped the team of five first-round draft picks, giving the team no natural pick in the draft from 2029 through 2033.TheNBAalso fined the Clippers $30m, and suspended owner Steve Ballmer from all league and team activities for a year. In addition, it issued suspensions without pay to president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank (six months) and president of business operations Gillian Zucker (one year) for their involvement in the scheme.Luka Dončić looks like a superstar adrift at the LakersRead moreLeonard was also fined $700,000. The Clippers agreed to trade the seven-time All-Star to the Toronto Raptors earlier this summer, but the deal had been put on hold pending the completion of the NBA’s investigation. Leonard is due to make $50m in salary this season, while Ballmer, the former CEO of Microsoft, has an estimated wealth of $152.7bn,according to Forbes.“The NBA’s collectively bargained system for determining player compensation is a fundamental component of the basketball competition that the league oversees for the benefit of the teams and players and ultimately the fans,” NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in a statement. “I am deeply disappointed by the flagrant violations of our rules and by the Clippers’ institutional and leadership failures that led to this misconduct. The severity of the penalties reflects the seriousness of the violations.”In a statement through his agent, Leonard said he took “full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any intent on anyone’s part to circumvent the salary cap.”The Clippers said they would challenge the investigation’s findings “through every avenue available to us” and looked “forward to an ethical and impartial arbitration process”.“We vehemently reject the NBA’s findings, which are the result of a heavily biased investigation seeking to justify a predetermined narrative rather than facts and evidence,” the team said in a statement. “What the league told us privately differs from what it announced today publicly, and they have not held themselves close to the standard Commissioner Silver set at the start of this investigation to ensure it’s fairness and accuracy.“For the past year, we cooperated fully and in good faith and we will now fight just as hard to demonstrate our innocence.”New York law firm Wachtell Lipton conducted the NBA’s investigation into the matter afterreporting by journalist Pablo Torre last year.Torre, citing legal documents, claimed Ballmer employed Leonard for a nonexistent role in a company Ballmer had invested in to circumvent the NBA salary cap, which punishes teams for spending too much on player salaries.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Weekly for the 2026 WNBA seasonSign up toWNBA 30A limited run women’s basketball newsletter dedicated to the league’s historic 30th season.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTorre claims that Ballmer partly funded a now defunct tree-planting company called Aspiration. That company then allegedly entered into a $28m agreement with KL2 Aspire, LLC, a company owned by Leonard.Torre says he could find no evidence that Leonard ever performed any work for Aspiration, and there was a clause in the contract between KL2 Aspire and Aspiration effectively allowed Leonard to be paid even if he did no work. Another clause said the deal would be voided if Leonard left the Clippers. One former employee of Aspiration told Torre he had heard the deal with Leonard had been set up to “circumvent the salary cap.”Wachtell Lipton’s reportconcluded that the Clippers broke NBA rules after “initiating off-court income opportunities between Mr Leonard and four companies doing business with the team: Aspiration Partners, Boingo Wireless, Daktronics, and Lockton Insurance; facilitating endorsement agreements between these companies and Mr Leonard; inducing the companies to enter into these agreements by offering them business from the team; paying personal expenses on behalf of Mr Leonard and his representatives; and failing to report improper solicitations for off-court income opportunities made on Mr Leonard’s behalf through his then-business manager, Dennis Robertson.”Leonard is one of the best players of his generation. The 35-year-old is a two-time NBA champion and was twice the league’s defensive player of the year. He started his career with the San Antonio Spurs before spells with the Raptors and Clippers.Leonard led the Clippers to the Western Conference finals in the 2020-21 season but they have failed to get beyond the first round of the playoffs since and missed the postseason entirely in 2025-26.Explore more on these topicsLos Angeles ClippersWest CoastNBABasketballUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: US cyclist Ezra Caudell hospitalized with ‘multi-system trauma’ after Philadelphia crash | Cycling | The Guardian
description: The 19-year-old American remains in hospital after being knocked unconscious in a collision during Sunday’s Philadelphia Cycling Classic
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: The 19-year-old American remains in hospital after being knocked unconscious in a collision during Sunday’s Philadelphia Cycling Classic
Content: Ezra Caudell (left) rides past the Philadelphia Museum of Art during the men’s Philadelphia Cycling Classic on Sunday.
